rationale: Both responses rest on the right core insight: MoE decouples stored from active parameters, so it saves compute and bandwidth but not memory. Both also misstate Mixtral 8x7B as 129B total parameters when it is about 47B, and B compounds the slip with a 70 GB Q4 figure. Beyond that shared error, B is more nuanced and actionable. It separates two latency regimes, a model that fits versus experts paged from disk, and adds the CPU cache-locality point. Its quantisation analysis is more specific: router sensitivity, non-uniform expert degradation and per-expert calibration scarcity, with a concrete tip to keep the router and attention at higher precision. Most importantly, it gives a memory-tiered decision framework that recognises small-active-parameter MoEs such as a 30B-A3B model as a real win on 32 GB machines. A's flat 'choose dense' conclusion misses that case. B also ties the recommendation to assistant-specific risks such as tool-calling and format adherence, and proposes a concrete evaluation on real prompts with p95 TTFT. Some of B's claims are speculative, but overall it is the stronger guide.
